tickets.title: US001 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to order food on my phone while walking from class, so that I can skip the cafeteria line.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Student can browse menu and place order via mobile.
- System generates order number and estimated pickup time.
- Confirmation message is displayed after successful order.

tickets.title: US002 (Chef/Staff)
tickets.description:
As a Chef, I want to mark an item as Sold Out instantly, so that students stop ordering unavailable food.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Staff can mark items as unavailable in real time.
- Changes are reflected immediately in student view.
- System logs all updates with timestamp and staff ID.

tickets.title: US003 (Student with Allergy)
tickets.description:
As a Student with a nut allergy, I want to filter the menu by allergens, so that I only see safe food options.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Student can select allergens to exclude (e.g., peanuts).
- Items containing selected allergens are hidden.
- Clearing filter shows all items again.

tickets.title: US004 (IT Infrastructure)
tickets.description:
As IT Staff, I want the kitchen display system to work offline for at least 10 minutes, so that orders are not lost during Wi-Fi outages.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Kitchen display continues to show recent orders without internet.
- Orders placed offline are queued locally.
- System syncs automatically once connection is restored.

tickets.title: US005 (Marketing Dept)
tickets.description:
As Marketing Staff, I want to send push notifications at 11:30 AM with discounts on the daily special, so that more students buy lunch.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Notification is sent at scheduled time.
- Message includes discount details and menu item.
- Students can opt in/out of marketing notifications.

analysis.ambiguity1: The kitchen needs a screen that shows orders as they come in.”\nWhy vague: The requirement does not specify how detailed the order display should be. It is unclear whether the screen must show only item names, preparation instructions, or customer details. Without clarification, developers cannot design the kitchen interface properly.\n
analysis.ambiguity2: Requirement: “The app should send push notifications to students at 11:30 AM offering them a discount on the daily special.” Why vague: The requirement does not define how discounts are calculated or applied. It is unclear whether the discount is a fixed percentage, a fixed amount, or varies by item. Without clarification, developers cannot implement the notification and pricing logic correctly.\n
analysis.conflictSolution: Conflict: The Cafeteria Manager wants mobile ordering to reduce queues, but the IT Infrastructure Team highlights unreliable Wi-Fi in the basement, which could disrupt the kitchen display system.\nResolution: The app will support offline caching for at least 10 minutes. Orders placed during outages will be stored locally and synced once the connection is restored. This ensures mobile ordering works smoothly while addressing infrastructure concerns.\n
analysis.nfr1: Usability: The menu filter must allow students with allergies to hide unsafe items completely, reducing stress and improving user experience.
analysis.nfr2: Performance: The system must update the kitchen display within two seconds of receiving a new order.
analysis.nfr3: Reliability: The kitchen display must continue to function offline for at least 10 minutes and sync seamlessly once the internet is restored.
